what_it_does: DRAM (dynamic random-access memory) chips in large cloud data centers occasionally develop errors. The standard response today is to migrate every virtual machine (a rented isolated computer environment) running on the affected physical server, even if the faulty memory region only overlaps with a small fraction of those virtual machines' working data. This paper introduces Pegasus, a system that maps the specific memory address ranges where errors are occurring onto the memory address ranges used by each individual virtual machine. A predictor then flags only those virtual machines whose data actually overlaps with the at-risk memory region, so only they need to be moved. This avoids disrupting the majority of tenants on a server just because one corner of its memory is becoming unreliable.
